newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes stronger in tight prompt supply.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes stronger in tight prompt supply.

text.p: North Sea crude spot prices and forward paper differentials surged higher on Thursday on the back of tight physical supplies, traders said.
Led by benchmark Dated Brent which traded over seven cents up on the last reported deal earlier in the week physical crudes across the North Sea all traded at stronger levels.
A wet Brent loading Feb 11-13 traded at March Brent +42 cents, up from Monday's highest trade of March +34.5 cents.
The benchmark was offered at March +45 cents late although the seller said he was considering withdrawing due to the strengthening Feb March spread which sold at +60 cents.
Despite the tightness at the front end of the market both of today's Brent cargoes loading Feb 14-16 were clocked.

Strength on other North Sea grades also confirmed the market's bullish tone. Statfjord traded at a firm Dated Brent +57 cents for a Feb 24-26 loader, a Forties cargo with end Feb loading options was done at Dated Brent +54 cents and an Oseberg loading Feb 19 moved at dated Brent +55 cents.
Traders said that simple supply/demand fundamentals had pushed premiums higher.
"There's a lack of avails and refiners need cover to keep running," said one major North Sea player.
"The U.S. and the Far East has been pulling quite a lot of oil out of the region," he added.

On paper, intermonth Brent spreads made strong gains. Feb/Mar gained over 10 cents with bids as high as +60. Mar/Apr traded up to +48 cents. March paper was valued around $23 a barrel at 1830 GMT in line with the IPE screen.
The Mediterranean too was stronger, two Urals deals confirmed earlier talk of a firmer market.
A large Urals cargo loading Feb 15-20 was bought by a European major at Dated Brent -65 cents, while another cargo with similar dates was sold to a refiner at Dated -67 cents.
